pppower 0.0.0.9000
  • Reference
  • Articles
    • Prediction-Powered Power Planning

    Monte Carlo Estimation of Empirical and Close-Form Power for PPI / PPI++ mean estimation

    ppi_empirical_power.Rd

    Runs a full Monte Carlo simulation for estimating power for the naive, PPI, or PPI++ estimators. Returns empirical rejection probability, Monte Carlo standard error, and theoretical (closed-form) power based on estimated population-level covariance components.

    ppi_empirical_power(
  R = 2000,
  n,
  N,
  X_sampler_L,
  X_sampler_U = NULL,
  f_generator,
  eps_sampler = function(n) rnorm(n, 0, 1),
  model_type = c("glm_correct", "glm_mis", "glm_wrong", "rf"),
  ppi_type = c("naive", "PPI", "PPI++"),
  lambda_mode = c("plugin", "theory"),
  lambda_external = FALSE,
  n_external = ceiling(n/2),
  alpha = 0.05,
  delta = 0,
  seed = NULL,
  pred_noise = 0,
  PPI_crossfit = FALSE,
  PPIpp_crossfit = TRUE,
  PPIpp_independent_split = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    R

    Number of Monte Carlo repetitions.

    n

    Size of labeled sample.

    N

    Size of unlabeled sample.

    X_sampler_L

    Function generating labeled covariates.

    X_sampler_U

    Function generating unlabeled covariates (defaults to X_sampler_L).

    f_generator

    Function generating signal mean function f(x).

    eps_sampler

    Error distribution sampler, default standard normal.

    model_type

    Choice of predictive model: "glm_correct", "glm_mis", "glm_wrong", "rf".

    ppi_type

    "naive", "PPI", or "PPI++".

    lambda_mode

    "plugin" or "theory".

    lambda_external

    Whether to estimate lambda on an external set.

    n_external

    Size of external set if used.

    alpha

    Significance level.

    delta

    True mean shift.

    seed

    Optional integer random seed for reproducibility.

    pred_noise

    Optional added prediction noise.

    PPI_crossfit

    Logical, use cross-fitting for PPI.

    PPIpp_crossfit

    Logical, use cross-fitting for PPI++.

    PPIpp_independent_split

    Logical, use 3-way independent split.

    Value

    A list containing:

    empirical_power

    Monte Carlo rejection rate

    mc_se

    Monte Carlo SE of empirical power

    theoretical_power

    closed-form population power

    avg_lambda_hat

    average estimated \(\hat\lambda\)

    cov_var_table

    tibble with covariance summaries used for power formula

    Examples

    ppi_empirical_power(
  R = 500,
  n = 100,
  N = 10000,
  X_sampler_L = function(n) data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n)),
  f_generator = function(X) 2 * X$x1,
  model_type = "glm_correct",
  ppi_type = "PPI"
)
